/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable language. A model $M$ of $T$ is *atomic*
if every finite tuple $\bar a$ of elements of $M$ realizes an isolated (principal) type over $T$:
there is a formula $\varphi(\bar x)$ true of $\bar a$ such that every formula $\psi(\bar x)$ true
of $\bar a$ satisfies $T \models \forall \bar x\,(\varphi(\bar x) \to \psi(\bar x))$.

The class $K$ of atomic models of $T$ is *categorical in $\lambda$* if $K$ has exactly one model
of cardinality $\lambda$ up to isomorphism. Since $K$ is not an elementary class, the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not provide models of every infinite cardinality, so existence of a
model of cardinality $\lambda$ is part of the definition.

Shelah's problem: if the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory (in a countable
language) is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in every
infinite cardinal? Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic assumption
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question in ZFC is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Shelah, *Classification theory for nonelementary classes. I. The number of uncountable models
  of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A and B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983), 212–240 and 241–273.
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, University Lecture Series 50, American Mathematical Society (2009).
-/

blocks.docstring:
A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `a` of elements of `M` realizes an
isolated (principal) complete type: there is a formula `φ` with `M ⊨ φ(a)` such that every
formula `ψ` with `M ⊨ ψ(a)` satisfies `T ⊨ ∀ x, (φ(x) → ψ(x))`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.CompleteType` / `Theory.typeOf` (Mathlib.ModelTheory.Types) — these give complete types as maximal theories in `L[[α]]`, but there is no notion of isolated/principal type there, and `BoundedFormula.IsAtomic` (Mathlib.ModelTheory.Complexity) is about atomic *formulas*, an unrelated concept.
justification.name: Categorical.IsAtomicModel
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of atomic model (every finite tuple realizes an isolated/principal complete type). Defined directly: for every `a : Fin n → M` there is a formula `φ` with `φ.Realize a` such that every `ψ` with `ψ.Realize a` satisfies `φ ⟹[T] ψ` (i.e. `T ⊨ ∀x (φ → ψ)`), which is the textbook definition (Marker, Baldwin).

blocks.name: IsAtomicModel
blocks.text:
/-- A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `a` of elements of `M` realizes an
isolated (principal) complete type: there is a formula `φ` with `M ⊨ φ(a)` such that every
formula `ψ` with `M ⊨ ψ(a)` satisfies `T ⊨ ∀ x, (φ(x) → ψ(x))`. -/
def IsAtomicModel (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n),
    φ.Realize a ∧ ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize a → φ ⟹[T] ψ

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomicModel.of_equiv {M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T} (hM : IsAtomicModel T M)
    (e : M ≃[L] N) : IsAtomicModel T N := by
  intro n a
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hψ⟩ := hM n (e.symm ∘ a)
  have ha : a = e ∘ (e.symm ∘ a) := by
    ext i
    simp
  refine ⟨φ, ?_, fun ψ hψ' => hψ ψ ?_⟩
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula]
    exact hφ
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula] at hψ'
    exact hψ'
blocks.docstring: Being an atomic model is invariant under isomorphism.
blocks.name: IsAtomicModel.of_equiv

/-- Being an atomic model is invariant under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomicModel.of_equiv {M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T} (hM : IsAtomicModel T M)
    (e : M ≃[L] N) : IsAtomicModel T N := by
  intro n a
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hψ⟩ := hM n (e.symm ∘ a)
  have ha : a = e ∘ (e.symm ∘ a) := by
    ext i
    simp
  refine ⟨φ, ?_, fun ψ hψ' => hψ ψ ?_⟩
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula]
    exact hφ
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula] at hψ'
    exact hψ'

def AtomicModelsCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M → IsAtomicModel T N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)
blocks.docstring:
The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ` and any two atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.
(Existence is part of the definition: the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not provide models of every infinite cardinality.)

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Cardinal.Categorical κ T` (Mathlib.ModelTheory.Satisfiability): all models of size κ are isomorphic; wrong class of models and no existence clause.
justification.name: Categorical.AtomicModelsCategorical
justification.why_needed: Categoricity in `κ` of the class of atomic models of `T`: existence of an atomic model of cardinality `κ` plus uniqueness up to `L`-isomorphism among atomic models of cardinality `κ`. Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical κ T` ranges over all models of `T`, and does not include existence (which matters here because the atomic class is not elementary). Two short proved `@[category API]` lemmas (`exists_isAtomicModel`, `of_categorical`) relate it to `Cardinal.Categorical`.

blocks.name: AtomicModelsCategorical
blocks.text:
/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ` and any two atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.
(Existence is part of the definition: the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not provide models of every infinite cardinality.) -/
def AtomicModelsCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M → IsAtomicModel T N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel {κ : Cardinal.{w}}
    (h : AtomicModelsCategorical T κ) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1
blocks.docstring:
If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`.
blocks.name: AtomicModelsCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel
blocks.text:
/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel {κ : Cardinal.{w}}
    (h : AtomicModelsCategorical T κ) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.of_categorical {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : κ.Categorical T)
    (h' : ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) :
    AtomicModelsCategorical T κ :=
  ⟨h', fun M N _ _ hM hN => h M N hM hN⟩
blocks.docstring:
If `T` is `κ`-categorical (in the sense of `Cardinal.Categorical`) and has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`, then the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`.
blocks.name: AtomicModelsCategorical.of_categorical
blocks.text:
/-- If `T` is `κ`-categorical (in the sense of `Cardinal.Categorical`) and has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`, then the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.of_categorical {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : κ.Categorical T)
    (h' : ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) :
    AtomicModelsCategorical T κ :=
  ⟨h', fun M N _ _ hM hN => h M N hM hN⟩

@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (T : L.Theory), Countable L.Symbols → T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicModelsCategorical T (ℵ_ n : Cardinal.{w})) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicModelsCategorical T κ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Shelah's problem on atomic classes.** Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable
language. If the class of atomic models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Here "categorical in $\lambda$" means that $T$ has an atomic model of cardinality $\lambda$ and
that all atomic models of $T$ of cardinality $\lambda$ are isomorphic. Since the countable atomic
model of $T$ is unique when it exists, this is the same as asking for categoricity in every
uncountable cardinal. Finite cardinals are excluded: a complete theory with an infinite model has
no finite models.

Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic assumption
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question in ZFC is open.

Here "categorical in $\lambda$" means that $T$ has an atomic model of cardinality $\lambda$ and

  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Shelah's problem, the ZFC version of Sh87a/b): 'the ℵ_n' means categorical in ℵ_n for every n < ω, the theory is implicitly in a countable language, 'every cardinal' means every infinite (equivalently every uncountable, since the countable atomic model is unique) cardinal, and categoricity in λ should include existence of a model of cardinality λ (the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so Löwenheim–Skolem does not give existence for free); the Prop is 'for every such T, categoricity in all ℵ_n implies categoricity in all infinite cardinals', with the yes/no answer as answer(sorry).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ countable L, complete T, (∀ n, atomic class categorical-with-existence in ℵ_n) → ∀ κ ≥ ℵ₀, categorical-with-existence in κ) and all compile. c06 was chosen as the base because (i) its atomic-model definition is the transparent textbook one (tuple realizes a type isolated over T, via `φ ⟹[T] ψ` = `T ⊨ᵇ φ.imp ψ`), (ii) it explicitly pins the model universe of the hypothesis (`ℵ_ n : Cardinal.{w}`) to that of the conclusion, and (iii) its names (`IsAtomicModel`, `AtomicModelsCategorical`) avoid shadowing Mathlib's order-theoretic `IsAtomic` (used by c03/c05). c01/c02/c07/c08 are mathematically equivalent (type-space isolation is equivalent by compactness) but let Lean generalize the hypothesis and the conclusion to *different* model universes (u_4 vs u_3), which is needlessly sloppy. c03/c04/c05 are equally faithful; I added c05's isomorphism-invariance API lemma (`IsAtomicModel.of_equiv`) to c06's file as an extra test of the bespoke definition.

context:
In mathematical logic, a theory is categorical if it has exactly one model (up to isomorphism). Such a theory can be viewed as defining its model, uniquely characterizing the model's structure.
In first-order logic, only theories with a finite model can be categorical, due to the upward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem. Higher-order logic contains categorical theories with an infinite model. For example, the second-order Peano axioms are categorical, having a unique model whose domain is the set of natural numbers $\mathbb {N} .$ In model theory, the notion of a categorical theory is refined with respect to cardinality. A theory is κ-categorical (or categorical in κ) if it has exactly one model of cardinality κ up to isomorphism. Morley's categoricity theorem is a theorem of stating that if a first-order theory in a countable language is categorical in some uncountable cardinality, then it is categorical in all uncountable cardinalities.
Saharon Shelah (1974) extended Morley's theorem to uncountable languages: if the language has cardinality κ and a theory is categorical in some uncountable cardinal greater than or equal to κ then it is categorical in all cardinalities greater than κ.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The decomposition table's reading (countable language, categoricity in every ℵ_n, existence included in categoricity, conclusion for every infinite cardinal, yes/no via answer(sorry)) agrees with the standard formulation of Shelah's problem and was followed exactly.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable language. A model $M$ of $T$ is *atomic*
if every finite tuple $\bar a$ of elements of $M$ realizes an isolated (principal) type over $T$:

infinite cardinal? Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic assumption
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question in ZFC is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Shelah, *Classification theory for nonelementary classes. I. The number of uncountable models
  of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A and B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983), 212–240 and 241–273.
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, University Lecture Series 50, American Mathematical Society (2009).
-/

namespace Categorical

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory)

/-- A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `a` of elements of `M` realizes an
isolated (principal) complete type: there is a formula `φ` with `M ⊨ φ(a)` such that every
formula `ψ` with `M ⊨ ψ(a)` satisfies `T ⊨ ∀ x, (φ(x) → ψ(x))`. -/
def IsAtomicModel (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n),
    φ.Realize a ∧ ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize a → φ ⟹[T] ψ

/-- Being an atomic model is invariant under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomicModel.of_equiv {M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T} (hM : IsAtomicModel T M)
    (e : M ≃[L] N) : IsAtomicModel T N := by
  intro n a
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hψ⟩ := hM n (e.symm ∘ a)
  have ha : a = e ∘ (e.symm ∘ a) := by
    ext i
    simp
  refine ⟨φ, ?_, fun ψ hψ' => hψ ψ ?_⟩
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula]
    exact hφ
  · rw [ha, StrongHomClass.realize_formula] at hψ'
    exact hψ'

/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ` and any two atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.
(Existence is part of the definition: the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not provide models of every infinite cardinality.) -/
def AtomicModelsCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M → IsAtomicModel T N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel {κ : Cardinal.{w}}
    (h : AtomicModelsCategorical T κ) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1

/-- If `T` is `κ`-categorical (in the sense of `Cardinal.Categorical`) and has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`, then the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.of_categorical {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : κ.Categorical T)
    (h' : ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) :
    AtomicModelsCategorical T κ :=
  ⟨h', fun M N _ _ hM hN => h M N hM hN⟩

/--
**Shelah's problem on atomic classes.** Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable
language. If the class of atomic models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Here "categorical in $\lambda$" means that $T$ has an atomic model of cardinality $\lambda$ and
that all atomic models of $T$ of cardinality $\lambda$ are isomorphic. Since the countable atomic
model of $T$ is unique when it exists, this is the same as asking for categoricity in every
uncountable cardinal. Finite cardinals are excluded: a complete theory with an infinite model has
no finite models.

Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic assumption
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question in ZFC is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (T : L.Theory), Countable L.Symbols → T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicModelsCategorical T (ℵ_ n : Cardinal.{w})) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicModelsCategorical T κ := by
  sorry

end Categorical

items: The list entry omits the language; following the decomposition notes and the standard statement of Shelah's problem (Baldwin, *Categoricity*; Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah), the theory is taken to be in a countable language, formalized as the hypothesis `Countable L.Symbols` (same idiom as `Wikipedia/VaughtConjecture.lean`).
'categorical in the ℵ_n' is read as categorical in ℵ_n for every n < ω: `∀ n : ℕ, AtomicModelsCategorical T (ℵ_ n)` using `Cardinal.aleph` with `n` cast to an ordinal (`ℵ_ 0 = ℵ₀`).

'every cardinal' is read as every infinite cardinal (`ℵ₀ ≤ κ`); finite cardinals are excluded because with existence built into categoricity no theory with infinite atomic models could be categorical there. The docstring notes that this is equivalent to categoricity in all uncountable cardinals since the countable atomic model is unique when it exists.

Categoricity in κ includes existence of an atomic model of cardinality κ (as the decomposition notes require), since the class of atomic models is not an elementary class and Löwenheim–Skolem does not give existence.

Atomic model is defined via isolation by a formula relative to `T` (`φ ⟹[T] ψ`, i.e. `T ⊨ᵇ φ.imp ψ`), quantifying over tuples indexed by `Fin n` for all n (including n = 0, where the condition is harmless for a complete T). Because `T` is complete, this is equivalent to isolation checked inside `M`.

Universes: `L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}`, models are `Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T` and cardinals are `Cardinal.{w}`; `ℵ_ n` is explicitly annotated as `Cardinal.{w}` so hypothesis and conclusion refer to models in the same universe. Since the language is countable, the universe of the model carrier is mathematically immaterial (any model of size κ can be shrunk/lifted to any universe containing κ).

`T.IsComplete` (Mathlib) includes satisfiability, matching 'complete first order theory'. `answer(True)` asserts the positive answer (the implication holds for every such T); `answer(False)` asserts a counterexample exists.

The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (inside `namespace Categorical`) rather than `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/` because the task permits writing only one file; a reviewer may prefer to move `IsAtomicModel` to `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/` as it is reusable.
References to Shelah's Sh:87a/b papers and Baldwin's book are given as plain text (no DOI links) to avoid unverified URLs; the required Wikipedia URL is included.

reviewer_notes: Reading adopted (matches the decomposition notes and the literature formulation of Shelah's problem, Sh87a/b, Baldwin 'Categoricity'): countable language (`Countable L.Symbols`, same idiom as Wikipedia/VaughtConjecture.lean); Mathlib `Theory.IsComplete` (satisfiable + semantically complete); 'the ℵ_n' = for every n : ℕ (Mathlib's `ℵ_ 0 = ℵ₀`, so n = 0 is included — harmless, since ℵ₁-categoricity with existence yields a countable atomic elementary substructure and the countable atomic model of a complete theory is unique); 'every cardinal' = every infinite cardinal (finite cardinals are impossible once T has infinite models; the ℵ₀ case follows from the hypothesis). Categoricity in κ includes existence of an atomic model of size κ, since the atomic class is not elementary; Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical` omits existence and would be vacuous where no atomic model exists. `T ⊨ᵇ` quantifies over models in universe max u v while the models in the categoricity clauses live in Type w; semantic consequence is universe-independent, so this is faithful. answer(True) asserts the positive (ZFC) answer to Shelah's question; answer(False) asserts a counterexample exists. Verified with `pp.universes` that the hypothesis and conclusion use the same model universe. Bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file because the task allows a single output file; `IsAtomicModel` is generic and a maintainer may prefer to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/. The Wikipedia article URL used is the one given in the background article.md (Categorical_%28model_theory%29).

title: Categoricity of the class of atomic models
